messages:
Maya (Support): Hi team, escalating a customer (NorseTech) on private deployment. They say requests set to eu-west-1 are being served from us-east-1 and incurring ~300ms p95. Billing shows tokens counted in us-east. Can infra/sre triage?

Ollie (Customer): Confirmed. We have an on-prem proxy (198.51.100.45) that peers to PartnerHub. We include X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 and our dashboard is set to eu-west-1. Still getting us-east responses. Screenshot of metrics attached to ticket.

Maya (Support): Can you paste minimal repro (curl) and any traceroute/tcpdump you can share?

Ollie (Customer): Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
```
Response headers show:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Served-Region: us-east-1
X-Request-ID: req_02Axxx
X-Redwood-Route: proxy-us-east
```
Trace:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (3.5.140.22), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.3 ms
 2  203.0.113.1  1.1 ms  <- on-prem proxy
 3  52.214.10.10  12.5 ms <- PartnerHub egress
 4  proxy-us-east.example.net (3.5.140.22)  220 ms
```
We also captured a tcpdump on the proxy: original client src 10.0.5.23 becomes 3.5.140.22 after SNAT at the hub.

Ravi (SRE): Hypothesis: PartnerHub SNATs peered traffic to an egress pool in us-east, so Redwood's region-selection (which uses source egress AS/ip mapping in our smart-router) is attributing the request to us-east. Two quick asks: (1) can PartnerHub share their NAT rule for that subnet, (2) do they manipulate BGP communities or override prefix announcements?

Lena (Infra): Also confirm: does the customer have a direct peering/pcx or is traffic hairpinned through a transit that then SNATs? That changes mitigation.

Ollie (Customer): We peer to PartnerHub (pcx-0abc) which forwards to internet via PartnerHub. No direct IGW from our VPC. PartnerHub said they NAT all forwarded traffic to an egress pool based on their default policy. They gave these details: NAT mapping had match source 198.51.100.0/24 -> SNAT pool egress-us-east (3.5.140.0/24). They said it was a catch-all and not region-aware.

Ravi (SRE): That matches the evidence. Our router determines 'served-region' based on observed egress IP mapping to our region-aware pools. Since the partner SNAT'd to us-east pool, requests are classified as us-east regardless of X-Redwood-Region header. Two remediation paths: short-term change at PartnerHub NAT to use egress-eu pool for that customer's source prefix, or we add a routing exception in our smart-router to prefer the dashboard/region header when the request is authenticated and a matching org ID is present.

Lena (Infra): Quick mitigation: I can request PartnerHub to change NAT mapping for 198.51.100.0/24 -> egress-eu (198.51.100.0 is our customer's announced pool). I've opened a ticket with them and asked for the change. Meanwhile, we can add a temporary mapping in our router to treat connections with X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 and valid org token as eu-west regardless of egress IP. That will require a small config change and tests.

DevOps Bot: change-request: add-router-exception (id: ch-20260317-07) created by Lena. Target: smart-router-ruleset.

Ravi (SRE): Before we flip config, can we reproduce in our lab? I simulated SNAT to us-east egress pool and verified the router resolves region from source IP -> us-east. Code path: src/router/region_lookup.go uses EgressIP->region map with fallback to header only for unauthenticated requests.

Maya (Support): Customer is asking for ETA. Can we give <2h for mitigation?

Lena (Infra): PartnerHub replied: they can update NAT mapping within 30 minutes for that prefix. They applied change: SNAT rule now maps 198.51.100.0/24 -> egress-eu pool (52.214.11.0/24). They also added logging.

DevOps Bot: config-change: PartnerHub applied NAT update for pcx-0abc. changeId: ph-20260317-03.

Ollie (Customer): Re-tested after ~90s:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Served-Region: eu-west-1
< X-Redwood-Route: direct-eu
```
Latency p95 back to ~55ms. Billing now attributes to eu-west. Thanks.

Ravi (SRE): Thanks. Follow-ups: (1) INFRA-1442: add a router rule that when requests include X-Redwood-Region and valid org token we prefer header-based routing for private peers (config flag off by default), (2) INFRA-1443: audit partner NAT rules for catch-all SNATs that map peered subnets to wrong egress pools, (3) add alert when >0.5% of requests for a regionorg show X-Served-Region mismatch with requested region.

Lena (Infra): I'll log INFRA-1442/1443 and coordinate with PartnerHub ops for a checklist. Also proposing partner onboarding document updates to require region-aware NAT or preserve-src.

Maya (Support): I'll reply to the customer with RCA: root cause = PartnerHub catch-all SNAT to us-east egress pool causing incorrect region classification; short-term fix = NAT remap; long-term = router header-preference toggle + partner checklist. Closing incident after customer confirms.

Ollie (Customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please keep us in the loop on the infra ticket so we can adjust our partner configs.

DevOps Bot: incident-closed: thread 1841002468 marked resolved. tickets: INFRA-1442, INFRA-1443.
